occupation.core_tool_quote: They use handtools, including squares, levels, and chisels, as well as many power tools, such as sanders, circular saws, nail guns, and welding machines.
occupation.not_claimed: No estimate of workers using this exact model or jam-clearing frequency.

steps.3: Lift the jam clear latch then pull up to open the nosepiece door.
steps.4: Remove bent nail, using pliers if necessary.
steps.5: If driver blade is in the down position, cycle the stall release lever.
steps.6: Close the nosepiece door and engage the latch pin under the two arms on the nosepiece. Push latch until it locks in place.

manufacturer.fixture_brad_length: 50mm authored stem (51.5mm bent-fastener longitudinal envelope), selected within supported range; not an OEM measured part

bounded_scope: Battery removed, trigger locked, magazine unloaded, driver already retracted. Lift latch/open door, extract a physically trapped pre-bent brad, close door and capture the bail pin under both arms, lock lever. No firing, driver reset, battery service or magazine refill.
geometry_provenance: Original benchmark-authored fixture geometry, joints/compliance/material/mass. Manufacturer does not document working dimensions or forces here. External door/lever/bail-pin/two-arm topology follows FigJ; effective elastic draw link is an explicit authored compliance surrogate, not a claim about hidden OEM internals.
orientation: Tool on its side; firing/nail axis+X away from robots, service normal-Y. Proper service-frame rotation is180deg aboutX; hinges open sideways in world coordinates.

novelty.comparison: Existing nailer task puts an unloaded rigid nailer in a case while avoiding pointing/trigger hazards; it has no jam clearing, nose door, articulated bail or fastener extraction.
novelty.accepted_comparator: detent-latch-bottle: related clasp/lid mechanics, different release goal. A generic clasp-only fixture is insufficient: implement real trapped bent-brad geometry and two-arm pin capture as essential physical constraints.
novelty.inventory: Scoped accessible public queries/catalog only; final review still required.

software_units_reference.basis: Angular stiffness and damping are per degree; scene.json and Isaac actuator configuration use per radian. USD coefficients=SI/(180/pi). This is software unit documentation, not manufacturer hardware evidence.
